clusters.name: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction

standards.skillName: Addition and Subtraction Word Problems within 20
standards.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing situations, with unknowns in all positions.
standards.ccssText: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

standards.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20.
standards.ccssText: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

clusters.name: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction

standards.description: Apply the commutative and associative properties of addition as strategies to add and subtract.
standards.ccssText: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract. Examples: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known. (Commutative property of addition.) To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12. (Associative property of addition.)

standards.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
standards.ccssText: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem. For example, subtract 10 – 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8. Add and subtract within 20.

standards.skillName: Counting On to Add and Subtract
standards.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction by counting on or counting back.
standards.ccssText: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

standards.description: Add and subtract within 20 using strategies such as making ten, decomposing, and using the relationship between addition and subtraction. Demonstrate fluency for addition and subtraction within 10.
standards.ccssText: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

clusters.name: Work with addition and subtraction equations

standards.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign and determine if addition and subtraction equations are true or false.
standards.ccssText: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false. For example, which of the following equations are true and which are false? 6 = 6, 7 = 8 – 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2.

standards.skillName: Finding the Unknown in an Equation
standards.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
standards.ccssText: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers. For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 + ? = 11, 5 = _ – 3, 6 + 6 = _.

domains.name: Number and Operations in Base Ten

standards.description: Count to 120 starting at any number, and read and write numerals to represent any number of objects within 120.
standards.ccssText: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

standards.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones, including the special cases of the numbers 11–19 and the multiples of 10.
standards.ccssText: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a "ten." The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones. The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

subStandards.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a "ten."
The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

standards.description: Compare two two-digit numbers using >, =, and < based on the meaning of the tens and ones digits.
standards.ccssText: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.

clusters.name: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract

standards.description: Add within 100, including a two-digit number plus a one-digit number and a two-digit number plus a multiple of 10, using place value strategies.
standards.ccssText: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

standards.description: Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than any two-digit number without counting, and explain the reasoning.
standards.ccssText: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

standards.description: Subtract multiples of 10 from multiples of 10 in the range 10–90, using place value strategies.
standards.ccssText: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

clusters.name: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units

standards.description: Order three objects by length and compare the lengths of two objects indirectly using a third object.
standards.ccssText: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

standards.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units by iterating shorter objects end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
standards.ccssText: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps. Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.

standards.skillName: Telling Time to the Hour and Half-Hour
standards.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.
standards.ccssText: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

standards.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about totals, category counts, and differences.
standards.ccssText: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

clusters.name: Reason with shapes and their attributes

standards.description: Distinguish defining attributes of shapes (number of sides, closed) from non-defining attributes (color, size, orientation); build and draw shapes with given defining attributes.
standards.ccssText: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

standards.description: Compose 2D and 3D shapes to create composite shapes, and compose new shapes from composite shapes.
standards.ccssText: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.

standards.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares and describe the shares using words like halves, fourths, and quarters.
standards.ccssText: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.
